subject: DPA clarifications - controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up & DPA questions from today's call

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Summary: Aurora is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing features that will process user-submitted documents (PII) and business metadata. You wanted clarification on data handling, retention, logging, and what we can commit to in the DPA.
- Action items: Redwood to provide written answers to controller/processor roles, subprocessors list, breach notice timing, and data residency options; Aurora to confirm any non-standard retention/erasure requirements.

Below are the specific questions you raised on the call — I'm pulling together formal answers and attaching our latest DPA for reference. Ben (cc) is our contracts/security point for any redlines.

1) For customer-submitted PII: does Redwood act as processor or controller?
2) What subprocessors do you use and will Aurora be notified of changes?
3) What is your breach notice timeline and escalation process?
4) Can we configure data residency and retention windows per environment?
5) Do you provide request-level logging and audit exports for compliance?

Attachment: DPA_Redwood_v2.pdf (summary + standard clauses)

Next: I'll consolidate Ben's legal answers and get back by end of day tomorrow. If you want to hop on a 15-min call with Ben, happy to set that up.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference platform for production LLMs
From: Samir Shah <samir@aurora-tech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karen Liu <karen.liu@aurora-tech.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & DPA questions from today's call

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap and the DPA. A couple of clarifications from our side so Ben can respond fully: 

- Controller/Processor: Our legal team wants a clear statement that Aurora is the controller for customer-submitted data and Redwood is the processor for any processing done on behalf of Aurora. Can you confirm the language in the DPA reflects that?
- Subprocessors: Can you provide the current list of subprocessors (cloud infra, analytics, monitoring) and confirm how you notify customers of additions/changes (notice period)?
- Breach notice: We typically require notification within 72 hours for incidents affecting PII. Is that aligned with Redwood's commitments?
- Logs & exports: Will we get request-level logs (timestamps, request IDs, model used) and regular audit exports? We need these for our SOC readiness.
- Data residency & retention: We plan to keep some customer content in US-only regions and need configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days plus option for manual purge).

If you can have Ben provide the formal responses and updates to the DPA, that would be great. Karen from our privacy team is cc'd — she'll jump in for legal edits.

Samir
VP Product, Aurora Tech
samir@aurora-tech.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@aurora-tech.com>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@aurora-tech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & DPA questions from today's call

Hi Samir / Karen —

Thanks for the clear list. I've pulled responses inline below and attached the DPA v2 with callouts: see sections 1.1 (roles), 3.2 (subprocessors), 5.1 (breach notice), and Appendix A (data residency/retention options).

1) Controller vs Processor
- Confirmed: Aurora Tech is the Controller and Redwood Inference is the Processor for all customer-submitted content. The DPA's Section 1.1 reflects this; we can add an explicit sentence if your counsel prefers exact phrasing.

2) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors: AWS (EC2/S3), Google Cloud (BigQuery for analytics), Sentry (error/monitoring), Segment (usage telemetry).
- Notice: We provide notification of material changes to the subprocessor list via email 30 days before onboarding any new subprocessor and allow customers to object on reasonable grounds. This is in Section 3.2.

3) Breach notice
- We commit to notify customers of confirmed security incidents affecting customer data within 72 hours of becoming aware, with an initial notification and follow-up updates. Our incident response playbook and escalation contacts are available on request. (Section 5.1)

4) Logs & audit exports
- We provide request-level logs (request ID, timestamp, model/version, endpoint, processing latency) and can provide weekly/monthly exports via secure S3 link or direct transfer. Retention of logs is configurable up to 13 months by plan; log retention shorter than 90 days can be requested as a custom option.

5) Data residency & retention
- Options: US-only region deployment (Redwood Private or Dedicated with region pinning) or hosted US-only for enterprise. Retention presets: 30/90/365 days or custom retention; manual purge API for immediate deletion. See Appendix A in attached DPA.

Attachment: DPA_Redwood_v2.pdf (with inline callouts)

If Aurora needs stricter breach SLA language (e.g., different notification windows or additional contractual remedies), we're open to discussing as a commercial term tied to contract tier. Marissa — happy to take this to a short call with Samir and Karen if helpful.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189
From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@aurora-tech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & DPA questions from today's call

Ben — thanks for the thorough responses and the DPA. A couple quick notes from Aurora legal after internal review: 

- Confirm controller/processor: language looks good; please add an explicit sentence in Section 1.1 stating "Aurora Tech is the Data Controller and Redwood Inference is the Data Processor with respect to customer-submitted content."
- Subprocessors: the listed subprocessors are acceptable. For the notice period, can we get 45 days instead of 30 for onboarding new subprocessors? We sometimes need additional review time for high-risk subprocessors.
- Breach notice: 72 hours initial notification is acceptable. We ask that the DPA include an explicit escalation contact list and one dedicated security liaison on Redwood's side for the duration of the relationship.
- Logs: please confirm the log export format (JSON lines preferred) and whether exports are hashed in transit.

If you can send an updated DPA with the explicit controller sentence, subprocessors notice window updated to 45 days, and the escalation contact added, we'll run a quick redline and aim to return within 3 business days.

Thanks — Karen
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Aurora Tech
karen.liu@aurora-tech.com
